correctness.rationale: Universal proof derives Pareto saturation of all jointly approved candidates, reduces EJR+ to two strict type-private quota inequalities, derives those inequalities from core+ reserve lower bounds, and constructs a type-symmetric payment certificate satisfying all four necessary and sufficient constraints. Strictification uses rational perturbations preserving strict capacity slack. Exact Python checker verifies 80,000 parameter instances (70,370 certificates, 9,630 necessary obstructions); finite tests support but do not replace proof. The non-Pareto boundary counterexample is checked exactly.

originality.rationale: Compared implications against the general core+ payment duality and unrestricted existence theorem (arXiv:2609.11912v2, Section 3, Theorem 3.2), the EJR+ axiomatics and witness conditions (arXiv:2605.04612v1, Section 2 and Appendix), and few-voter-type ordinary core existence (arXiv:2605.06194v2, introduction, principal results and concluding discussion). General existence is existential and does not classify each Pareto-efficient EJR+ committee. Earlier two-ballot FJR+ classifications also do not force the strictly stronger fractional core+. No covering implication was located; risk of an unindexed domain theorem remains.
residual_risks: Unindexed earlier equivalence or alternate frugal Lindahl-priceability theorem may cover the two-type characterization.

The parameter-range result is not independently peer validated.

value.rationale: A natural approval-elections domain with overlapping voter types collapses a stronger fractional coalition-stability notion to a simple representation quota condition on every Pareto-efficient committee. The constructive rational certificate resolves a genuine membership/classification question, and the sharp two-voter counterexample explains why efficiency matters. This goes beyond repeating the general core-existence result.
